key_facts.fact: The Great Fire of London started on September 2, 1666 in Thomas Farriner's bakery on Pudding Lane
The fire burned for 4 days, destroying 13,200 houses, 87 churches, and most of the City of London
Samuel Pepys buried his Parmesan cheese and wine to save them from the fire
Only 6 deaths were officially recorded, though the true number is likely higher
Christopher Wren was charged with rebuilding many significant parts of the city, including St. Paul's Cathedral

strongest_angle: The Great Fire of London wasn't just a disaster—it was a story of human error, institutional failure, and remarkable resilience. From Samuel Pepys burying his cheese to the Lord Mayor's catastrophic decision-making, the fire reveals how a city's character is forged in crisis.
